title: Issue, Loading and Activation of Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers
content:
## 1. Instrument fixed by the ground of issue

The instrument of a Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers credit is fixed by its ground of issue and each instrument's grounds of issue:

| Ground of issue | Instrument issued |
|---|---|
| exchange residual | Crestline Residual Travel Credit |
| voluntary or involuntary cancellation | Crestline Flight Credit |
| refund taken as credit | Crestline Trip Credit |
| service recovery | Crestline Service Recovery eCertificate |
| irregular-operations goodwill | Crestline Disruption Voucher |
| denied-boarding compensation | Crestline Denied Boarding Voucher |

A credit redeposit returns value from a refunded or cancelled ticket that was paid with a credit. It is issued as the same instrument as the credit that paid, and where the instrument's value is returned with the original expiry date it keeps that credit's expiry date.

## 2. Name, face value and expiry date

- Every credit is issued in the traveler name of the passenger on the source ticket.
- The face value is rounded as the instrument's face value rounding provides, and a value below the instrument's minimum face value is not issued at all.
- The expiry date is the expiry anchor plus the instrument's validity months in calendar months. The anchor is the original ticket issue date for an instrument whose validity counts from the original ticket issue date, and the credit issue date for an instrument whose validity counts from the credit issue date. Adding months keeps the day of the month, and falls back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist.

*Hypothetical expiry dates, 12 months of validity:* an anchor of 15 April 2025 gives 15 April 2026; an anchor of 29 February 2024 gives 28 February 2025, because 29 February does not exist in 2025.

## 3. Loading and activation

Issuing a credit loads its face value in one load entry. A credit that becomes usable automatically is active immediately after the load. A voucher that becomes usable on passenger acceptance becomes active only when the passenger accepts it in place of cash.

## 4. Acceptance window

A voucher can be accepted only within the instrument's acceptance window, in calendar days after the voucher was issued. The window is counted in calendar days from the issue date on the credit record, and acceptance on the last day of the window is accepted. The issue date the system records is the evidence; the check concerns this voucher. A voucher not accepted by then is voided, and the cash compensation is paid instead under the ticket rules of Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.

| Hypothetical voucher with a 14-day window, issued 1 June | Result |
|---|---|
| Accepted on 15 June (day 14) | Accepted; the voucher becomes active |
| Accepted on 16 June (day 15) | Outside the window; the voucher is voided and cash compensation is paid instead |

## 5. Credit issued in error

A credit issued in error may be voided only while it is still issued, before any use.
